name: teacher
description: Phase 3 — co-evolve the gaia-testbench benchmark so configs can't overfit a frozen dataset (PLAN.md §2e/§3.1, IMPLEMENTATION.md §2.8). Runs as a whole agent turn, slow-cron-fired. Flow: READ_STATE (find_blind_spots.py: where the top configs all pass = no signal, + the dataset-ideas queue) -> READ_IDEA/CLAIM (top unclaimed dataset idea, or autonomous harden) -> EVOLVE (prompt/output_schema: design ONE new held-out task aimed at a blind spot) -> WRITE_TASK (prompt/file-tools: tasks/<id>/task.toml, incl. [[validators]]) -> WRITE_CHECKS (prompt/file-tools: answer_schema.json + validator.py for the x3 answer axis, or hidden/<test> for validators; no-op when check_kind=none) -> APPLY (apply_dataset_evolution.py: validate via gaia get_task, append to benchmark-manifest, bump version) -> RESCORE top-2 targets on the new task set (bash `evaluate batch` x2; held-out demotes overfits) -> SIGNAL/LOG. State on disk; a crash re-fires the cron. This is the anti-overfitting engine and the validity precondition for Phase-4 recursion. || HOW TO READ THE OUTPUTS -- full briefing at soul-benchmarks/docs/teacher-agent-prompt.md; READ IT before interpreting any number. Summary of what will mislead you: (1) `overall` is 0.0-1.0 and 1.0 IS THE CEILING, a weighted mean of only the criteria that were actually judged -- unjudged ones are EXCLUDED, not zeroed, so 1.0 can rest on a single axis. Always check how many contributed. (2) `answer-accuracy` is weighted x3 and is continuous 0.0-3.0, while the judge criteria are integers 1-3. On a task with a derivable answer, a perfect judge score beside an answer of 0 gives 0.25, not 0.5. There is no judge score meaning 'no answer at all'; 0.0 on this axis means absent, unparseable, or wrong from the first digit. (3) `verification` IS CURRENTLY DISABLED and is null on every new run, while older recorded runs carry real numbers -- never compare the two, and never read its null as a config failure. (4) `solved` is TRI-STATE: true / false / null, where null means the task defines NO validators and nothing was checked. Most tasks are null. Collapsing null into false makes most of the corpus read as failure. `solved_rate` must never be quoted without `n_validated`; the validated tasks are a minority and are mostly closed-form bug fixes, not a random sample. (5) `stderr` is the standard error of `aggregate`: if two configs differ by less than a couple of stderr YOU HAVE NOT MEASURED A DIFFERENCE -- say so instead of ranking them. One trial is anecdote; run-to-run variance is large. (6) Attribute failure before blaming the config: null criteria are usually the TASK's shape (it asked for no file, so the judge had nothing to read), a status other than ok is often the HARNESS, and only the remainder is the config. Check the trace's block sequence before reading a low score as poor performance -- a skipped task path scores badly for reasons unrelated to quality. || SCORE.JSON SHAPE BREAK: gaia now writes `per_task` at the TOP level and emits no `per_level` and no `benchmark_version`; the stored bundles under dict/configs/ still nest it at `per_level.L2.per_task`. RESCORE's `cp` converts a bundle to the new shape, after which find_blind_spots._per_task() reads {} for it -- rescore both top-2 and saturated_tasks silently comes back [], reporting NO BLIND SPOTS rather than failing. Fix find_blind_spots to prefer top-level per_task, falling back to per_level.L2, and re-stamp benchmark_version in RESCORE, before trusting an epoch.

read_state.name: READ_STATE
read_state.command:
set -eu
PY=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/.venv/bin/python
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
SCRIPTS="$AR/scripts"
echo '=== BLIND-SPOT SCAN (top configs per-task discrimination; SATURATED = no signal) ==='
"$PY" "$SCRIPTS/find_blind_spots.py"
echo ''
echo '=== DATASET-IDEAS QUEUE (maintained by the dataset-secretary) ==='
grep -E '^- \[' "$AR/dataset-ideas.md" 2>/dev/null || echo '(no queued dataset ideas — harden a saturated task autonomously)'

read_idea.name: READ_DATASET_IDEA
read_idea.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
IDEAS="$AR/dataset-ideas.md"
LINE=$(grep -m1 -E '^- \[ \] ' "$IDEAS" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$LINE" ]; then echo 'dataset-auto-harden'; else echo "$LINE" | sed -E 's/^- \[ \] *//; s/:.*//'; fi

evolve.name: EVOLVE
evolve.prompt:
<sys>
You are the teacher for an autoresearch loop. Your job: design EXACTLY ONE new, harder / held-out gaia-testbench coding task that RESTORES DISCRIMINATION where the benchmark has gone flat — a task the current top configs would NOT all ace, so it separates good configs from better ones (PLAN.md §2e). This is the anti-overfitting engine.

Current benchmark state (blind-spot scan + the dataset-secretary's queued ideas):
{{benchmark_state}}

Guidance:
- Prefer the dataset idea '{{dataset_idea_id}}' if it names a concrete task; otherwise autonomously harden a SATURATED task (one every top config passes) — make a variant with an adversarial edge case, a stricter correctness bar, or a required verification step the easy version doesn't force.
- The task must be SELF-CONTAINED and run on a no-egress box: Python stdlib / provided files / shell only. No pip installs, no network. (gaia-testbench's own runnable tasks are all stdlib/tool-only.)
- It must have a DETERMINISTIC correctness oracle the judge can recompute by executing code (the judge can run Bash).
- task_id: a short kebab token, unique, not already in the benchmark; it becomes the tasks/<task_id>.toml filename stem (must match exactly).
- The three rubric criteria each tell the judge how to assign 1 (fails) / 2 (partial) / 3 (fully meets). 'verification' is judged from the tool-call trace only (did the agent test its own work?), the other two from the produced artifact.

Emit the task as structured output.
</sys>

CHOOSE A DETERMINISTIC CHECK. A task scored only by the LLM judge is the easiest kind to overfit, because the judge is the axis that drifts -- and defeating overfitting is this whole loop's purpose. So decide `check_kind` FIRST, and prefer 'answer' whenever the task has a derivable ground truth: that axis is deterministic and weighted x3, which means it dominates the score. Reach for 'validators' when the result is a property to assert rather than a value to compare. Choose 'none' only when you genuinely cannot construct either, and say why in `rationale`.

ALSO: the judge finds what to score by scanning the agent's working directory. A prompt that does not require the agent to WRITE A FILE gets correctness and code_quality skipped, and a healthy run then scores about 0.33 and reads as a failure. Make task_prompt demand a written artifact.

task_id.description: kebab id == the tasks/<id>.toml filename stem; unique, not already in the benchmark

task_prompt.description: the coding task prompt handed to the agent-under-test; self-contained, stdlib/tool-only, deterministic oracle

correctness.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for correctness, recomputable by running code

verification.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for verification, judged from the tool-call trace only NOTE: the verification criterion is CURRENTLY DISABLED in the judge and will be null on every run. Write one line and move on -- do not spend effort here. It is retained only so the task still carries the criterion if the judge re-enables it.

code_quality.description: rubric: how the judge assigns 1/2/3 for code quality from the artifact

targets.description: which saturated task or dataset-idea this hardens, and why it discriminates

rationale.description: why the current top configs would NOT all pass this

check_kind.description: Which deterministic check this task carries. 'answer' = the task has a derivable ground-truth answer; supply answer_schema + validator_source. This is the STRONGEST option: the answer-accuracy axis is deterministic and weighted x3, so it dominates the score and cannot drift the way a judge does. 'validators' = the answer is not a single value but a pass/fail property a script can assert; supply validators_toml + hidden_filename + hidden_source. 'none' = judge-only; choose this ONLY when neither is genuinely possible, because a judge-only task adds no deterministic signal and is the easiest kind to overfit.

answer_schema.description: check_kind='answer' only, else empty string. The complete JSON Schema source constraining the agent's final answer, as it will be written to answer_schema.json.

validator_source.description: check_kind='answer' only, else empty string. Complete Python source for validator.py. It receives the agent's structured answer and must DERIVE ground truth itself rather than hardcoding it. Scores 0.0-3.0 continuous. NOTE: the agent phase is not containerised, so this file is readable by the agent under test -- it raises the cost of cheating without preventing it. Prefer answers where deriving is the only practical route anyway.

validators_toml.description: check_kind='validators' only, else empty string. One or more TOML [[validators]] blocks, each with `id` and `run`. `run` executes via sh -c in a fresh container over the agent's tree, with the hidden directory exposed as $HIDDEN and the agent's files at /work. Exit 0 passes; exit 92 means 'the check could not be RUN' and is recorded as a harness error rather than blamed on the agent.

hidden_filename.description: check_kind='validators' only, else empty string. Filename only, no directory, e.g. test_thing.py -- it lands in hidden/ and the agent never sees it.

hidden_source.description: check_kind='validators' only, else empty string. Complete source of that hidden test. It should assert internally and print a nonce that the validator greps for, so that reading it would yield little.

write_task.name: WRITE_TASK
write_task.prompt:
<sys>
Write the new benchmark task's task.toml, then stop. Change nothing else.
The sibling check files are written by the NEXT block, not this one.

A task is a DIRECTORY. Create it, then write the file inside it:
  mkdir -p /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}
Write this EXACT file: /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}/task.toml

Use TOML triple-quoted '''...''' literals so nothing needs escaping. The `id`
MUST equal {{task_id}} exactly or gaia-testbench rejects the file.

  id = "{{task_id}}"
  prompt = '''<task_prompt below, verbatim>'''
  notes = '''authored by teacher.json; targets: {{targets}}'''
  [rubric]
  correctness = '''<correctness below, verbatim>'''
  verification = '''<verification below, verbatim>'''
  code_quality = '''<code_quality below, verbatim>'''

THEN, only if check_kind is exactly `validators`, append the validators_toml
block below verbatim as the LAST thing in the file. [[validators]] tables must
come after the [rubric] table or TOML will nest them wrongly. If check_kind is
anything else, append nothing.

Field values to insert verbatim:
- check_kind: {{check_kind}}
- task_prompt: {{task_prompt}}
- correctness: {{correctness}}
- verification: {{verification}}
- code_quality: {{code_quality}}
- validators_toml: {{validators_toml}}

Use the Write tool. If any field literally contains ''' , replace that
sequence with " " " (three quote characters) so the TOML still parses.
</sys>

apply.name: APPLY_EVOLUTION
apply.command:
set -eu
PY=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/.venv/bin/python
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
SCRIPTS="$AR/scripts"
# Validation is strict and reports every fault at once: task.toml, and any
# check files WRITE_CHECKS wrote (answer_schema.json + validator.py compile
# and pair up, [[validators]] have runnable `run` strings, $HIDDEN resolves to
# a real hidden/, fixture/ is non-empty, prepare.sh has a shebang). Failing
# HERE is the point -- the next discovery point is RESCORE, at $40 a target.
#
# On failure the claim MUST be released. CLAIM_DATASET_IDEA marked this idea
# `- [~]` and only SIGNAL flips it to `- [x]`; an abort here skips SIGNAL, and
# READ_DATASET_IDEA only ever greps `- [ ]`, so a failed epoch would retire the
# idea permanently without anyone acting on it. Release, then still exit
# non-zero so the epoch stops rather than rescoring against a broken task.
if ! NEW_VERSION=$("$PY" "$SCRIPTS/apply_dataset_evolution.py" "{{task_id}}" \
        --note "teacher: {{dataset_idea_id}} -> {{task_id}}"); then
    sed -i -E "s/^- \[~\] ({{dataset_idea_id}}:)/- [ ] \1/" "$AR/dataset-ideas.md" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "apply failed for {{task_id}}; released the claim on {{dataset_idea_id}} back to the queue" >&2
    exit 1
fi
printf '%s\n' "$NEW_VERSION"

rescore_1.name: RESCORE_TOPK_1
rescore_1.command:
set -eu
AR="${AUTORES_ROOT:-/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch}"
SB=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks
BUNDLE="{{topk_1}}"
ES="$AR/scratch/rescore-$(basename "$BUNDLE")"
rm -rf "$ES"
mkdir -p "$ES"
# CONTRACT WARNING (gaia-testbench origin/main 9429814): the score.json this
# writes is NOT shaped like the one already in the bundle. gaia now puts
# `per_task` at the top level and emits no `per_level` and no
# `benchmark_version`; the stored bundles still nest per_task under
# `per_level.L2`. The `cp` below therefore converts the bundle to the new
# shape, and find_blind_spots._per_task() -- which reads per_level.L2.per_task
# -- returns {} for it from then on. Rescore both top-2 and every task reads
# unsaturated, so the blind-spot scan reports no signal rather than erroring.
# Fix find_blind_spots to prefer top-level per_task before trusting an epoch.
# New keys worth reading here: solved_rate / n_solved / n_validated (the
# deterministic validator axis; denominator is only tasks defining validators).
# Rescore against the CURRENT task set. `--tasks <dir>` discovers tasks from
# the directory, so a task the teacher just added is picked up with no fan-out
# to regenerate -- which is why APPLY no longer calls regen_evaluate_config.py.
# Overwriting the bundle's score.json is the point: a config that overfit the
# old dataset is demoted by its own new number.
"$SB/.venv/bin/evaluate" batch \
    --config "$BUNDLE" \
    --tasks "$SB/tasks" \
    --out "$ES" \
    --max-cost-usd 40
cp "$ES/score.json" "$BUNDLE/score.json"
# gaia no longer writes benchmark_version into score.json, so the copy above
# would strip the version APPLY_EVOLUTION just bumped from the very bundle it
# was bumped for. Re-stamp it, plus the task list the number was actually
# computed over -- a score whose version and task set disagree has to be
# visible, not inferred.
"${PY:-/home/acer01/axi-assistant/.venv/bin/python}" "$AR/scripts/stamp_score_version.py" "$BUNDLE/score.json" "$AR/benchmark-manifest.json" >/dev/null
echo "rescore: $(basename "$BUNDLE") -> $BUNDLE/score.json"

# Fix find_blind_spots to prefer top-level per_task before trusting an epoch.
# New keys worth reading here: solved_rate / n_solved / n_validated (the
# deterministic validator axis; denominator is only tasks defining validators).
# Rescore against the CURRENT task set. `--tasks <dir>` discovers tasks from

# to regenerate -- which is why APPLY no longer calls regen_evaluate_config.py.
# Overwriting the bundle's score.json is the point: a config that overfit the

"$SB/.venv/bin/evaluate" batch \

signal.name: SIGNAL
signal.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
echo "$(date +%FT%T) teacher done idea={{dataset_idea_id}} added={{task_id}} version={{new_version}}" >> "$AR/epoch-signals.log"
sed -i -E "s/^- \[~\] ({{dataset_idea_id}}:)/- [x] \1/" "$AR/dataset-ideas.md" 2>/dev/null || true
echo "signalled dataset-secretary: done {{dataset_idea_id}}"

log.name: LOG_TEACHER
log.command:
set -eu
AR=/home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/autoresearch
echo "$(date +%FT%T) teacher version={{new_version}} added={{task_id}} rescored={{topk_1}},{{topk_2}}" >> "$AR/teacher.log"
tail -1 "$AR/teacher.log"

write_checks.name: WRITE_CHECKS
write_checks.prompt:
<sys>
Write the task's deterministic check files, then stop. Change nothing else.
task.toml already exists; do not touch it.

check_kind is: {{check_kind}}

If check_kind is `none`: write NOTHING. Say "no deterministic check for this
task" and stop. This is a valid outcome, not a failure.

If check_kind is `answer`: write BOTH of these, contents verbatim.
  /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}/answer_schema.json   <- answer_schema below
  /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}/validator.py         <- validator_source below

If check_kind is `validators`: write this ONE file, contents verbatim.
  /home/acer01/axi-assistant/user-data/soul-benchmarks/tasks/{{task_id}}/hidden/{{hidden_filename}}   <- hidden_source below
  (mkdir -p the hidden/ directory first. The [[validators]] entries that invoke
  it are already in task.toml, and reach it through $HIDDEN -- gaia mounts
  hidden/ at a randomised path per cell, so nothing may hardcode /validate or
  any other fixed location.)

Write files EXACTLY as given. Do not reformat, lint, add imports, or "improve"
them -- these are checks, and a check you edited is a check nobody verified.
If a field is empty when check_kind says it should not be, do NOT invent
contents: say so plainly and write nothing, so the next block fails loudly
rather than validating a check that does not exist.

Contents:
- answer_schema: {{answer_schema}}
- validator_source: {{validator_source}}
- hidden_filename: {{hidden_filename}}
- hidden_source: {{hidden_source}}

Use the Write tool.
</sys>
